interpretive.rule: Original creditors (banks collecting own debts) are 'debt collectors' under §1788.2(c) — foundational case establishing California's expansion beyond federal FDCPA
Collection litigation misconduct (filing without documentation, false pleadings) violates §1692e incorporated via §1788.17; emotional distress damages recoverable
§1788.30(b) includes punitive damages under §3294 for egregious collection conduct — Rosenthal's primary damages advantage over federal FDCPA

operational_notes_for_steward_cases.forum_selection: California state court preferred for Rosenthal claims when: (1) collector is original creditor (avoids FDCPA's third-party limitation), (2) concrete-injury showing for Article III standing would be weaker (avoids Spokeo/TransUnion), (3) punitive damages are viable (§1788.30(b) + §3294 available in state court).
auto_fraud_checklist: Identify every collection communication from each auto dealer or assignee finance company
Was the collection notice the first communication? Did it include mini-Miranda (§1692e(11) via §1788.17)?
Was a validation notice sent within 5 days (§1692g via §1788.17)?
Did any communication falsely represent the contract was legally enforceable? (It was voidable under Rees-Levering §2981.9 — false representation of legal status = §1692e(2)(A) via §1788.17)
Did collection continue after written dispute? (§1692g violation via §1788.17)
Was any collection threat made that could not legally be carried out? (§1788.15)
operational_notes_for_steward_cases.punitive_damages_theory: For auto dealer defendants: if the dealer's standard practice was to use Rees-Levering-non-compliant multi-document contracts AND then collect on them (knowing the contracts were voidable), that pattern is malicious/oppressive conduct supporting §3294 punitive damages via §1788.30(b). Discovery into the dealer's standard form contracts and collection practices is the vehicle for punitive evidence.
operational_notes_for_steward_cases.sol: 1 year from date of violation. California Civ. Code §1788.30(f). Each collection communication is a new violation with its own 1-year clock.
